DIR_AIMO3_UTILS = '/kaggle/input/notebooks/harrysun2006/aimo-3-utils'

def set_env(input_archive, temp_dir):
    if not os.path.exists(temp_dir):
        os.makedirs(temp_dir, exist_ok=True)
        subprocess.run(['tar', '-xzf', input_archive, '-C', temp_dir], check=True)
    subprocess.run([
        sys.executable, 
        '-m', 
        'pip', 
        'install', 
        '--no-index', 
        '--find-links', 
        f'{temp_dir}/wheels', 
        'unsloth', 
        'trl', 
        'vllm', 
        'openai_harmony',
    ], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, check=True)

set_env(
    input_archive=f'{DIR_AIMO3_UTILS}/wheels.tar.gz',
    temp_dir='/kaggle/tmp/setup'
)
```

# Per-competition kernel config — single source of truth for ALL nemo variants.
#
# Modelled on tools/legacy/kkr.yaml: `_base` holds shared fields; each section
# overrides only what differs. `kernel-metadata.json` is generated on the fly at
# push/submit time (not source-controlled) via:
#
#   python tools/kca/yaml_meta.py build competitions/nvidia-nemotron/kca-nemo.yaml <section> \
#       --src-dir competitions/nvidia-nemotron/kernels --out <build_dir>
#   python tools/kca/kca.py kaggle push --kernel-dir <build_dir> --no-watch
#   # on COMPLETE:
#   python tools/kca/kca.py kaggle submit --competition nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge \
#       --kernel <id> --version <v> --file submission.zip --message "..."
#
# `id` carries the account (harrysun2006 = "harry", firefly2006 = "may"); per-team
# submission quota (5/day) is shared across both accounts.
#
# Annotation keys (lb / schedule / note) are ignored by the metadata generator;
# they document results and the run cadence (see README "Scheduling").

_base:
  competition: nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge

# %%
SHARD = 1  # account B
USE_SOUP = False  # B: classic RFT from base (no soup; firefly2006 lacks the private soup dataset)
CATEGORIES = ["bit", "equation", "cipher"]  # hardest categories (where SFT plateaus)
N_PROMPTS = 1200  # prompts to sample this shard
N_SAMPLES = 4  # samples per prompt
SAMPLE_MAX_TOKENS = 4096
TEMPERATURE = 0.8
import time as _time

T0 = _time.time()
SAMPLE_DEADLINE_SEC = 25200  # 7h wall-clock guard; always reach the save

# %%
import json
import math
import re
import subprocess

import kagglehub

# vLLM must be importable offline; if not, try the attached offline wheels, else fail-fast.
try:
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
    for _wd in glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/wheels", recursive=True) + glob.glob(
        "/kaggle/input/**/packages", recursive=True
    ):
        subprocess.run(
            ["pip", "install", "-q", "--no-index", "--find-links", _wd, "vllm"],
            check=False,
        )
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
print("vllm", vllm.__version__)

MODEL_PATH = kagglehub.model_download(
    "metric/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b-bf16/transformers/default"
)
SOUP_PATH = None
if USE_SOUP:
    _cfg = glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/adapter_config.json", recursive=True)
    assert _cfg, "USE_SOUP but soup adapter not found under /kaggle/input"
    SOUP_PATH = os.path.dirname(_cfg[0])
_train = glob.glob("/kaggle/input/competitions/*/train.csv") or glob.glob(
    "/kaggle/input/**/train.csv", recursive=True
)
assert _train, "train.csv not found"
print("model:", MODEL_PATH, "| soup:", SOUP_PATH, "| train:", _train[0])

# %%
# official-metric extract + verify (binary string-matched; numeric within 1e-2)
_BOXED = re.compile(r"\\boxed\{([^}]*)(?:\}|$)")
_LZ = re.compile(r"0\d+")


def extract_final_answer(text):
    if not text:
        return "NOT_FOUND"
    m = _BOXED.findall(text)
    if m:
        ne = [x.strip() for x in m if x.strip()]
        return ne[-1] if ne else m[-1].strip()
    nums = re.findall(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?", text)
    return nums[-1] if nums else "NOT_FOUND"


def verify(gold, pred):
    gold, pred = str(gold).strip(), str(pred).strip()
    if not _LZ.fullmatch(gold) and not _LZ.fullmatch(pred):
        try:
            return math.isclose(float(pred), float(gold), rel_tol=1e-2, abs_tol=1e-5)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            pass
    return pred.lower() == gold.lower()


def classify(p):
    pl = p.lower()
    if "8-bit binary" in pl or "bit manipulation" in pl:
        return "bit"
    if "gravitational constant" in pl:
        return "gravity"
    if "unit conversion" in pl or "convert the following measurement" in pl:
        return "unit"
    if "secret encryption" in pl or "decrypt" in pl:
        return "cipher"
    if "numeral system" in pl:
        return "numeral"
    if "transformation rules is applied to equations" in pl:
        return "equation"
    return "other"


# %%
import csv

rows = [
    r
    for r in csv.DictReader(open(_train[0], encoding="utf-8"))
    if classify(r["prompt"]) in CATEGORIES
]
rows = [r for i, r in enumerate(rows) if i % 2 == SHARD][:N_PROMPTS]  # shard split
print(f"shard {SHARD}: {len(rows)} prompts over {CATEGORIES}")

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest

llm = LLM(
    model=str(MODEL_PATH),
    tensor_parallel_size=1,
    max_num_seqs=64,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,
    dtype="auto",
    max_model_len=8192,
    trust_remote_code=True,
    enable_lora=USE_SOUP,
    max_lora_rank=32,
)
tok = llm.get_tokenizer()
SUFFIX = (
    "\nPlease put your final answer inside \\boxed{}. For example: \\boxed{your answer}"
)
lora = LoRARequest("soup", 1, SOUP_PATH) if USE_SOUP else None


def build_prompt(p):
    return tok.apply_chat_template(
        [{"role": "user", "content": p + SUFFIX}],
        tokenize=False,
        add_generation_prompt=True,
        enable_thinking=True,
    )


# fail-fast: one prompt must load+generate before the full shard
_sp1 = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=512)
_o = llm.generate([build_prompt(rows[0]["prompt"])], _sp1, lora_request=lora)
assert _o and _o[0].outputs, "fail-fast: vLLM+LoRA produced no output"
print("preflight OK; sample text:", _o[0].outputs[0].text[:120].replace("\n", " "))

# %%
sp = SamplingParams(
    temperature=TEMPERATURE, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=SAMPLE_MAX_TOKENS, n=N_SAMPLES
)
kept = []
BATCH = 64
for i in range(0, len(rows), BATCH):
    if _time.time() - T0 > SAMPLE_DEADLINE_SEC:
        print("wall-clock budget hit; stopping sampling")
        break
    batch = rows[i : i + BATCH]
    outs = llm.generate(
        [build_prompt(r["prompt"]) for r in batch], sp, lora_request=lora
    )
    for r, out in zip(batch, outs):
        for cand in out.outputs:
            if verify(r["answer"], extract_final_answer(cand.text)):
                kept.append(
                    {
                        "id": r["id"],

===== insights.md =====
# Insights — nemo

## Competition-specific insights
- **Faithful replay of the public 0.86/0.87 recipe is the single biggest lever** (0.67→0.85): CCE +
  MoE 128-expert weight tying + LoRA on `lm_head`/`in_proj`/`out_proj` + seq8192 + huikang recording-order
  corpus + replay-math answer tokens. Evidence: issue #86 T10 / comment 2.
- **Any "augmentation" on top of the clean replay recipe dilutes it** — T7 merge (0.82) and v15 cryptarithm
  synth (0.84) both regressed. Weight-space merge only helps among comparable, complementary adapters;
  strong+weak dilutes. Evidence: issue #86 comments 3–4.
- **Single-category gains ≠ total-score gains**: cryptarithm 8%→71% single still left total ~0.86.
  Evidence: issue #86 T11 / comment 4.
- **CoT supervision must land at the sequence tail and survive truncation** (`</think>\n\boxed{}`);
  right-truncation at small seq destroys it (ctx2k → 0.42). Evidence: issue #86 T2 / comment 0.

- **response-only loss masking is the key to CoT SFT**: training the loss over prompt+padding (v6) collapsed to 0.44; masking the prompt (labels=-100, response-only) recovered it (v7 0.65). Evidence: `bugs.md` B2 / issue #86 comment 0.
- **CoT traces must precompute every intermediate value (no inline arithmetic) and end with a finality line**: v10's short rule-traces made greedy reasoning shallow (0.59); v15's generator fixed this (CoT-answer consistency 1930/1930). Evidence: issue #86 T4 / T11; `work/00.nemo.md` ideas A/B.

## Potentially reusable insights

### INS-001: push-time static lint + single-example fail-fast preflight
- type: rule
- confidence: high
- evidence: `kernels/README.md`; issue #86 (F821 / `.shape` each cost ~2h GPU)
- transfer scope: any GPU kernel / long training competition
- status: candidate (logged in `_shared/skill-candidates.md`)

### INS-002: eval harness must mirror the official metric (decode length + extractor)
- type: anti-pattern
- confidence: high
- evidence: issue #86 T12/T13 (EVAL_MAX_NEW 512→7680; port official extract/verify)
- transfer scope: any hidden-test LLM/eval competition
- status: candidate
- notes: misaligned local eval gives misleading scores (cf. orbit-wars self-play vs ladder).

### INS-003: weight-space adapter merge only among comparable, complementary adapters
- type: fact
- confidence: medium
- evidence: issue #86 T7 / comment 3 (strong+weak SVD merge regressed)
- transfer scope: multi-checkpoint LoRA/adapter ensembling
- status: validated (this competition)

# Postmortem: context consolidation (nemo, 2026-06-14)

> KCT-002: consolidated the long issue-#86 tracking context into English canonical docs under
> `competitions/nvidia-nemotron/`. Builds on KCT-001 (PR #100). Chinese originals preserved as `_zh` sidecars.
> The original KCT-001 postmortem is preserved (English) in [`2026-06-14-kct-001-initial-consolidation.md`](./2026-06-14-kct-001-initial-consolidation.md).

## Sources read
- GitHub issue **#86** (body + 5 comments; Chinese strategy/tracking hub) — primary.
- `work/00.nemo.md` (ChatGPT competition analysis, zh); `work/00.nemotron_3_versions.zip` (3 ChatGPT scripts, names only).
- `worklogs/nemo.md`, `worklogs/nemo2.md`; `experiments/kernel/README.md`; PRs #90/#94/#95.
- `experiments/synth/nemo_synth_gen.py`, `experiments/merge/svd_merge.py`, `kernels/*/kernel-metadata.json` (also indexed in `references.md`).

## Key facts recovered
- Submit rank≤32 LoRA adapter (Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B, Mamba+MoE); greedy `max_tokens=7680, temp=0`;
  extract `\boxed{}` (exact or numeric 1e-2); metric accuracy; 9 reasoning categories; train ~9500; hidden test.
- Deadline 2026-06-15 23:59 UTC; 5 submissions/team/day; top ~0.89; base ~0.47.
- LB progression: v5 0.61 → v7 0.65 → ctx4k 0.67 → v10 0.59 → **v14 replay 0.85 (best)** → T7 merge 0.82 → v15 synth 0.84.

## Decisions recovered
- D1–D9 all confirmed 2026-06-12 (see `tracking.md` Table 1). Merge scope = own adapters only (D3); #85 tooling post-comp (D6); seq8192 + ≤8h guard (D9).
- Closing recommendation (comment 4): **hold 0.85**.

## Open blockers
- 0.85 appears to be the ceiling with current levers; beating it likely needs undisclosed top-tier tricks.

## Active tasks recovered
- Hold 0.85 to deadline; optional half-dose cryptarithm-only synth (user-decides).

## Known submissions/results recovered
- See `submissions.md` / `tracking.md` (kernel push + LB table). Private LB `unknown`.

## Bugs recovered
- See `bugs.md` (ctx2k truncation, v6 masking, BatchEncoding fail-fast, eval truncation T13, ptxas, data glob, timeout, cryptarithm single≠total).

## Reusable insights
- Faithful public-recipe replay is the dominant lever; augmentations dilute it; eval harness must mirror the
  official metric; push-time lint + fail-fast preflight. See `insights.md` / `_shared/`.

## Chinese→English translations performed
- Issue #86 Tables 1–3 (D1–D9, T1–T13, References) → `tracking.md` (EN). Comments 2/4 key conclusions → EN in `tracking.md`/`strategy.md`/`insights.md`.
- Interim Chinese KCT-001 docs (README/rules/strategy/tasks/submissions/bugs/references/insights) → rewritten English canonical.

## _zh sidecars created
- `tracking_zh.md` (verbatim issue #86 body, Chinese 3 tables), `notes_zh.md` (zh source pointers + key comment excerpts).

## Uncertain or missing context
- Private LB; exact submission IDs; exact train row count; `test.csv`=first-3-train claim (as reported).
- Read-only Kaggle status **refreshed 2026-06-14** (both accounts via `kaggle competitions submissions`; all submissions `COMPLETE`). Best own real-training = 0.85 (v14); raw account public max = 0.86 (2026-05-15 public-fork); leaderboard top ~0.90. Private LB not released. The Kaggle submissions API exposes no numeric submission ID (date+description is the key).

## Proposed follow-up issues
- "nemo: post-deadline archival" (finalize LB/CV + private LB + final postmortem; status → archived).
- "nemo: port official metric + min-logprob hard-val set (T12)".

## 1. Final recommendation (as written at audit time): hold 0.85
Two principled attempts to beat 0.85 both regressed (T7 merge 0.82, v15 synth 0.84); `insights.md`:
any augmentation on top of the clean replay recipe dilutes it. The one high-EV unbuilt lever
(bit/equation solver-distillation, `work/00.nemo.md` §10②) is high-risk. **LB keeps the max → 0.85 is
banked and safe.** (User subsequently approved a best-effort last-window swing at B + C — §10.)

⚠ Open verification: which submissions are selected for private scoring is `unknown`. Raw account public
max is **0.86** but from a **2026-05-15 public-fork (repack, not own training)** — touches the self-imposed
no-repack red line. Own-work best = **0.85 (v14)**.

the public recipe); the plan's most-touted lever (bit/equation solver synth) was never built; everything we did
build on top of v14 (v10/v15/t7) underperformed it.

## 4. Deep dive
### 4a. bit manipulation
- **Candidate-function enumeration solver: NOT implemented.** No solver searches a function library against
  example pairs (grep: no `def solve`/enumeration loop on real prompts).
- v10 emits a template for bit (`nemo-rule4k-v10.py:257-259`: "Compare each 8-bit example bitwise…") — no compute.
- v15 `make_bit_puzzle` (`nemo_synth_gen.py:178`) is a **generator** (`rng.sample(ops,2-4)` → known rule → CoT
  verifies the known ops), not a solver of an unknown rule.
- English prompts: yes (`ALICE_HEADER`, :17). Synth volume: bit only **150/2640 (~5.7%)** in v15 (`DEFAULT_MIX`).
- Validation: bit not in the exact-match consistency check (it is self-consistent by construction).
- Result: no per-category LB (`unknown`); v15 overall 0.84 < 0.85. **Plan called bit the biggest lever; it got the least.**

### 4b. equation / symbol
- Split exists **only in the synthetic generator**: `equation_numeric_deduce` (f(x)=ax+b/quadratic/floor/arith/geom,
  :927) + `_guess` (sequences, :1019); `make_symbol_puzzle` (5-char bijection, :521); `cryptarithm_deduce/guess`
  (:781/:805). **No real-prompt solver split** — v10 lumps all into one "equation" bucket (:162) with a template.
- Pure symbol strings: operands are fixed **2 chars** (`_make_sym_operand`, :603); operators `+-*/` map to **8 fixed
  string-rewrite rules** (`_RULE_REGISTRY`, :574). **No variables / functions / arbitrary-length tokens.**
  `force_unknown` only injects unseen **chars** (:647).
- Exact-output risk: symbol/cryptarithm use exact string match (CoT-answer consistency 1930/1930 covers self-
  consistency, but the fixed small rule set may mismatch the hidden test distribution); numeric categories carry
  rounding risk (same family as B1).

## 6. Synthetic / solver audit
- Generated: 10 deterministic puzzle+long-CoT categories (`PUZZLE_MAKERS`, :1088); v15 used 2640, cryptarithm 60%
  (deduce 900 + guess 700), equation_numeric 200×2, bit/symbol 150, encrypt 100, numeral/unit/gravity 80
  (`DEFAULT_MIX`, :1103).
- Ratio: ~24% of v15 training (interleaved ~1 per 3).
- Verification: exact-category CoT-answer consistency **1930/1930** (`validate()`), but **generator self-consistency,
  not real-prompt solving**.
- Dilution: ~24% synth slightly diluted other categories (B8); single-cat ≠ total.
- Cryptarithm result: v15 = **0.84** < 0.85 — did not deliver.
- Real solver: **none** (Idea A/D/E solvers never built).

## 8. Bug / failure lessons (`bugs.md`)
- **B1** seq2048 right-trunc cut `</think>\n\boxed{}` tail → 0.42.
- **B2** no response-only masking → 0.44.
- **B3** `apply_chat_template(tokenize=True)` BatchEncoding → `len()` on dict keys → 0 samples (public 0.87 notebook
  may never have run).
- **B4** held-out eval `EVAL_MAX_NEW=512` truncated → misleading local; → 7680 + EVAL_TIME_CAP=1800s.
- **B5** ptxas-blackwell non-executable → copy /tmp + chmod + monkeypatch.
- **B6** data at `/kaggle/input/competitions/<slug>/` → glob, no hardcode.
- **B7** v9 wall-clock overrun → TrainerCallback stop + guaranteed save/zip.
- **B8** (wontfix) cryptarithm single-cat gains ≠ total (8%→71% single, total still ~0.86).
- **B9** (obsolete) v7 NameError / v8 `.shape` each cost ~2h → push-gate ruff F821 + fail-fast preflight.

## 9. Last-~10h options table (at audit time)
| Option | Expected LB | Upside | Downside | GPU time | Quota | Impl risk | Recommend? |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. hold 0.85 | 0.85 | none | none | 0 | 0 | none | ✅ (default) |

| C. bit/equation real solver-distillation | unknown (theoretical max) | medium (only untried high-EV) | build+run risk | ~7–8h | 1 | high | ❌ at audit (time) |
| D. different-weight re-merge | ≤0.85 | none (only one strong adapter) | 1 quota | ~0.5h | 1 | low | ❌ |
| E. v11 rejection-sampling self-distill | unknown | medium | multi-session sampling | many | many | high | ❌ |

### 9b. Additional directions surfaced in PR #106 review
| Option | Idea | Assessment | Recommend? |
|---|---|---|---|
| G. **Mine real equation/cryptarithm rules → expand solver** | the C-solver's fixed rewrite library only matched **0.4%** of real `equation` prompts; reverse-engineer the actual per-operator rules from train.csv to lift coverage, yielding *verified real-prompt* cryptarithm CoT (vs synthetic) | The strongest untried cryptarithm angle: real, verified, on-distribution. Caveat B8 (single-cat ≠ total) still applies. ~3–4h build + 1 kernel | ⚠ worth a slot if C1/C2 don't beat 0.85 |
| H. **Better merge — only if a 2nd *strong* adapter appears** | T7 failed because it merged strong+weak (dilution, INS-003). A merge can only help among *comparable, complementary* members | We have exactly **one** strong adapter (v14). If an in-flight b/c kernel lands ≈0.85 on *different* data, a v14+that merge becomes worth trying. **NB: the submission is a SINGLE rank-≤32 LoRA — the eval loads one `lora_path`; "a collection of adapters" is only submittable by merging them into one (= T7), not as an ensemble.** | ⚠ conditional on a 2nd strong adapter |
| I. **Teacher-model distillation of CoT** | use a strong external reasoner to generate CoT toward the *known* train answers, SFT the Nemotron LoRA on it (richer than the base-model self-distill of T5/v11), esp. for bit/equation where the deterministic solver coverage is thin | Plausible higher-quality hard-category data. The adapter stays a Nemotron LoRA (you distill *outputs*, not weights). ⚠ verify comp rules permit external-model-generated training data; needs a capable teacher (local coder LLMs aren't strong puzzle reasoners) | ⚠ verify rules first; medium-effort |

## 10. Post-audit decision (user-directed)
With **~33h** actually remaining (clock 2026-06-14 14:42 UTC) — not ~10h — the timeline objection to option C
relaxes. User approved a best-effort last-window swing: **2 pushes per account (harry + may) attempting B and C**,
submit on completion. Safety: each is a fresh rank-32 LoRA on the v14 backbone (no repack); the C solver keeps only
prompts where its computed answer **matches the train.csv ground truth** (cannot poison); LB keeps the max so 0.85 is
never at risk. Variants + results tracked in `tracking.md` / `submissions.md`.

@dataclass
class Plan:
    name: str
    idea: str
    milestones: list[str]
    python_tasks: list[str]
    risk: str
    verification: list[str]

    def summarize(self) -> str:
        ms = "\n".join(f"- {m}" for m in self.milestones)
        py = "\n".join(f"- {t}" for t in self.python_tasks) if self.python_tasks else ""
        ver = "\n".join(f"- {v}" for v in self.verification)
        out = [f"Plan[{self.name}]: {self.idea}", "Milestones:", ms]
        if py:
            out += ["Python tasks (n<=200):", py]
        out += ["Risk:", f"- {self.risk}", "Verify:", ver]
        return "\n".join(out)

@dataclass

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Patch a live nemo-v11 kernel notebook: replace the vLLM offline-bootstrap cell
with one that extracts the aimo-3-utils wheels bundle and pip-installs vLLM.
Also adds the aimo-3-utils utility kernel to kernel_sources in metadata.

Usage: patch_kernel.py <kernel_dir> <ipynb_name>
"""
import glob
import json
import sys

KDIR = sys.argv[1]
UTILS_KERNEL = "harrysun2006/aimo-3-utils-0171"

NEW_CELL = '''# vLLM offline bootstrap: vLLM is absent from the base image. Extract the
# aimo-3-utils wheels bundle (py3.12 / cu128 / vllm 0.17.1) and pip-install
# vLLM with --no-index from that single clean wheels dir (mirrors the proven
# gpt-oss set_env; do NOT --find-links the read-only nvidia util mount).
try:
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
    _arch = sorted(
        glob.glob("/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/aimo-3-utils*/wheels.tar.gz")
        + glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/wheels.tar.gz", recursive=True)
    )
    assert _arch, "aimo-3-utils wheels.tar.gz not attached (add it as a kernel source)"
    _setup = "/kaggle/tmp/setup"
    if not os.path.exists(_setup + "/wheels"):
        os.makedirs(_setup, exist_ok=True)
        subprocess.run(["tar", "-xzf", _arch[0], "-C", _setup], check=True)
    subprocess.run(
        ["pip", "install", "-q", "--no-index", "--find-links", _setup + "/wheels", "vllm"],
        check=True,
    )
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
print("vllm", vllm.__version__)
'''

ipynb_path = glob.glob(f"{KDIR}/*.ipynb")[0]
nb = json.load(open(ipynb_path))

patched = 0
for c in nb["cells"]:
    if c["cell_type"] != "code":
        continue
    s = "".join(c["source"])
    if "import vllm" in s and "except Exception" in s:
        c["source"] = NEW_CELL.splitlines(keepends=True)
        # strip outputs/exec count so the push is clean
        c["outputs"] = []
        c["execution_count"] = None
        patched += 1

assert patched == 1, f"expected 1 vllm cell, patched {patched}"
json.dump(nb, open(ipynb_path, "w"), indent=1)
print(f"patched {patched} cell in {ipynb_path}")

# metadata: add the utils kernel source
meta_path = f"{KDIR}/kernel-metadata.json"
meta = json.load(open(meta_path))
ks = meta.get("kernel_sources", [])
if UTILS_KERNEL not in ks:
    ks.append(UTILS_KERNEL)
meta["kernel_sources"] = ks
json.dump(meta, open(meta_path, "w"), indent=2)
print("kernel_sources ->", ks)

```

"""Patch a live nemo-v11 kernel notebook: SURGICALLY replace the vLLM
try/except bootstrap (keeping any imports that precede it in the same cell)
with one that extracts the aimo-3-utils wheels bundle and pip-installs vLLM.
Also adds the aimo-3-utils utility kernel to kernel_sources in metadata.

Usage: patch_kernel.py <kernel_dir>
"""
import glob
import json
import sys

KDIR = sys.argv[1]
UTILS_KERNEL = "harrysun2006/aimo-3-utils-0171"

NEW_BOOTSTRAP = '''# vLLM offline bootstrap: vLLM is absent from the base image. Extract the
# aimo-3-utils wheels bundle (py3.12 / cu128 / vllm 0.17.1) and pip-install
# vLLM with --no-index from that single clean wheels dir (mirrors the proven
# gpt-oss set_env; do NOT --find-links the read-only nvidia util mount).
try:
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
    _arch = sorted(
        glob.glob("/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/aimo-3-utils*/wheels.tar.gz")
        + glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/wheels.tar.gz", recursive=True)
    )
    assert _arch, "aimo-3-utils wheels.tar.gz not attached (add it as a kernel source)"
    _setup = "/kaggle/tmp/setup"
    if not os.path.exists(_setup + "/wheels"):
        os.makedirs(_setup, exist_ok=True)
        subprocess.run(["tar", "-xzf", _arch[0], "-C", _setup], check=True)
    subprocess.run(
        ["pip", "install", "-q", "--no-index", "--find-links", _setup + "/wheels", "vllm"],
        check=True,
    )
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
print("vllm", vllm.__version__)
'''

ipynb_path = glob.glob(f"{KDIR}/*.ipynb")[0]
nb = json.load(open(ipynb_path))

patched = 0
for c in nb["cells"]:
    if c["cell_type"] != "code":
        continue
    s = "".join(c["source"])
    if "import vllm" in s and "except Exception" in s:
        # Keep everything before the `try:` that introduces the vllm import.
        idx = s.index("try:")
        prefix = s[:idx]
        new_src = prefix + NEW_BOOTSTRAP
        c["source"] = new_src.splitlines(keepends=True)
        c["outputs"] = []
        c["execution_count"] = None
        patched += 1

assert patched == 1, f"expected 1 vllm cell, patched {patched}"
json.dump(nb, open(ipynb_path, "w"), indent=1)

meta_path = f"{KDIR}/kernel-metadata.json"
meta = json.load(open(meta_path))
ks = meta.get("kernel_sources", [])
if UTILS_KERNEL not in ks:
    ks.append(UTILS_KERNEL)
meta["kernel_sources"] = ks
json.dump(meta, open(meta_path, "w"), indent=2)

# Echo the patched cell + preceding-import check for verification.
codes = ["".join(c["source"]) for c in nb["cells"] if c["cell_type"] == "code"]
vi = next(i for i, x in enumerate(codes) if "aimo-3-utils" in x)
before = "\n".join(codes[:vi]) + "\n" + codes[vi].split("try:")[0]
print(f"== {ipynb_path} ==")
for m in ["import os", "import glob", "import subprocess"]:
    print(f"  {m} present before vllm install: {m in before}")
print("  kernel_sources ->", ks)

```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Poll both v11 kernels every 180s. Exit early when a decisive signal appears:
#  - either kernel ERROR/COMPLETE (terminal), OR
#  - both RUNNING for >=4 consecutive checks (~12 min => env/preflight passed).
set -u
HARRY_CFG="$HOME/.kaggle"
running_streak=0
for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  TS=$(date -u +'%H:%M:%SZ')
  A=$(KAGGLE_CONFIG_DIR="$HARRY_CFG" kaggle kernels status harrysun2006/nemo-v11-sample-a2 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'KernelWorkerStatus\.[A-Z]*' | head -1)
  B=$(KAGGLE_CONFIG_DIR=/tmp/nonexistent_kcfg KAGGLE_USERNAME=firefly2006 KAGGLE_KEY=8d9**************************b73 kaggle kernels status firefly2006/nemo-v11-sample-b 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'KernelWorkerStatus\.[A-Z]*' | head -1)
  echo "[$TS] check#$i  A2(harry)=$A  B(may)=$B"
  case "$A $B" in
    *ERROR*|*COMPLETE*|*CANCEL*) echo "DECISIVE: terminal status reached"; exit 0;;
  esac
  if [ "$A" = "KernelWorkerStatus.RUNNING" ] && [ "$B" = "KernelWorkerStatus.RUNNING" ]; then
    running_streak=$((running_streak+1))
  else
    running_streak=0
  fi
  if [ "$running_streak" -ge 4 ]; then
    echo "DECISIVE: both RUNNING for ~12 min (env/preflight passed)"; exit 0
  fi
  sleep 180
done
echo "watch loop ended (timeout)"

```

> Based on the search results, here's what I found about vLLM's support for Nemotron-H and hybrid Mamba2 architecture:
> 
> ## Support Status
> 
> Recent work in the vLLM community has elevated hybrid models from experimental hacks in V0 to fully supported first-class citizens in V1. Hybrid models like Nemotron Nano 2 are architectures that combine attention with alternatives such as Mamba, and this support was a significant development.
> 
> ## Release Details
> 
> With the release of the vLLM V1 engine, hybrid models, like Nemotron-Nano-9B-v2, have become first-class citizens. Recent work in the vLLM community has elevated hybrid models from early experimental implementations to fully supported, high-class citizens.
> 
> ## Practical Implementation
> 
> Users have been running Nemotron Nano 9B v2 Japanese on vLLM 0.15.1, and vLLM has native Mamba support via --mamba_ssm_cache_dtype float32.
> 
> The key architectural challenge was managing different state requirements: Attention layers rely on a paged KV cache, organized into 16-token blocks. Mamba layers maintain a large, fixed-size state for each sequence that is updated in place rather than appended to.

> Root cause is clearer now: the bootstrap **got past** the tar-extract and ran my `pip install`, but pip failed with the **same read-only error** — `Read-only file system: '/kaggle/usr/lib/notebooks/ryanholbrook/nvidia_utility_script/nvidia/nccl/include/'`. The `ryanholbrook/nvidia-utility-script` mount (needed for the Blackwell ptxas/cutlass fix) puts a **read-only `nvidia/` namespace on `sys.path`**, so a normal install tries to merge the `nvidia-*` wheels (torch's CUDA deps) into that read-only dir and dies. The gpt-oss kernel never hit this because it doesn't attach that util script.
> 
> Fix: install the vLLM closure into a dedicated writable dir with `--target` + `--ignore-installed` and prepend it to `sys.path` — pip then writes everything into the target and never touches the read-only mount. Let me re-pull fresh and apply this.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Patch a live nemo-v11 kernel notebook: replace the vLLM bootstrap with one
that installs the aimo-3-utils wheels into a writable --target dir (avoiding the
read-only ryanholbrook nvidia namespace) and prepends it to sys.path.
Preserves the genuine import lines; strips any prior bootstrap comment block.
Adds the aimo-3-utils utility kernel to kernel_sources.

Usage: patch_kernel.py <kernel_dir>
"""
import glob
import json
import sys

KDIR = sys.argv[1]
UTILS_KERNEL = "harrysun2006/aimo-3-utils-0171"

NEW_BOOTSTRAP = '''# vLLM offline bootstrap. vLLM is absent from the base image; install it from the
# aimo-3-utils wheels bundle (py3.12 / cu128 / vllm 0.17.1). Install the closure
# into a dedicated writable dir with --target and prepend it to sys.path: the
# ryanholbrook/nvidia-utility-script mount puts a READ-ONLY `nvidia/` namespace on
# sys.path, so a normal install fails trying to merge the nvidia-* (torch CUDA)
# wheels into it. --target keeps every file inside /kaggle/tmp/pyenv.
import sys

_PYENV = "/kaggle/tmp/pyenv"
if _PYENV not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _PYENV)
try:
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
    _arch = sorted(
        glob.glob("/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/aimo-3-utils*/wheels.tar.gz")
        + glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/wheels.tar.gz", recursive=True)
    )
    assert _arch, "aimo-3-utils wheels.tar.gz not attached (add it as a kernel source)"
    _setup = "/kaggle/tmp/setup"
    if not os.path.exists(_setup + "/wheels"):
        os.makedirs(_setup, exist_ok=True)
        subprocess.run(["tar", "-xzf", _arch[0], "-C", _setup], check=True)
    subprocess.run(
        [
            "pip", "install", "-q", "--no-index",
            "--find-links", _setup + "/wheels",
            "--target", _PYENV, "--ignore-installed",
            "vllm",
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
print("vllm", vllm.__version__)
'''


def strip_trailing_comments(prefix: str) -> str:
    lines = prefix.splitlines()
    while lines and (lines[-1].strip() == "" or lines[-1].lstrip().startswith("#")):
        lines.pop()
    return "\n".join(lines)


ipynb_path = glob.glob(f"{KDIR}/*.ipynb")[0]
nb = json.load(open(ipynb_path))

patched = 0
for c in nb["cells"]:
    if c["cell_type"] != "code":
        continue
    s = "".join(c["source"])
    if "import vllm" in s and "except Exception" in s:
        prefix = strip_trailing_comments(s[: s.index("try:")])
        new_src = (prefix + "\n\n" + NEW_BOOTSTRAP) if prefix else NEW_BOOTSTRAP
        c["source"] = new_src.splitlines(keepends=True)
        c["outputs"] = []
        c["execution_count"] = None
        patched += 1

assert patched == 1, f"expected 1 vllm cell, patched {patched}"
json.dump(nb, open(ipynb_path, "w"), indent=1)

meta_path = f"{KDIR}/kernel-metadata.json"
meta = json.load(open(meta_path))
ks = meta.get("kernel_sources", [])
if UTILS_KERNEL not in ks:
    ks.append(UTILS_KERNEL)
meta["kernel_sources"] = ks
json.dump(meta, open(meta_path, "w"), indent=2)

codes = ["".join(c["source"]) for c in nb["cells"] if c["cell_type"] == "code"]
cell = next(x for x in codes if "aimo-3-utils" in x)
print(f"== {ipynb_path} ==\n{cell}\nkernel_sources -> {ks}\n")

```

  sleep 180
done
echo "watch loop ended (timeout)"
EOF

# aimo-3-utils wheels bundle (py3.12 / cu128 / vllm 0.17.1). Install the closure
# into a dedicated writable dir with --target and prepend it to sys.path: the

# vLLM offline bootstrap. vLLM is absent from the base image; install it from the
# aimo-3-utils wheels bundle (py3.12 / cu128 / vllm 0.17.1) into a dedicated
# writable dir with --target, then put it FIRST on sys.path. Two pitfalls handled:
#  (1) the ryanholbrook/nvidia-utility-script mount puts a READ-ONLY `nvidia/`
#      namespace on sys.path, so a plain install fails merging nvidia-* (torch
#      CUDA) wheels into it -> --target keeps every file in /kaggle/tmp/pyenv.
#  (2) inserting a not-yet-existent dir on sys.path poisons the import finder
#      cache -> insert AFTER install and call importlib.invalidate_caches().
import importlib
import sys

_PYENV = "/kaggle/tmp/pyenv"
try:
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
    _arch = sorted(
        glob.glob("/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/aimo-3-utils*/wheels.tar.gz")
        + glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/wheels.tar.gz", recursive=True)
    )
    assert _arch, "aimo-3-utils wheels.tar.gz not attached (add it as a kernel source)"
    _setup = "/kaggle/tmp/setup"
    if not os.path.exists(_setup + "/wheels"):
        os.makedirs(_setup, exist_ok=True)
        subprocess.run(["tar", "-xzf", _arch[0], "-C", _setup], check=True)
    os.makedirs(_PYENV, exist_ok=True)
    subprocess.run(
        [
            "pip", "install", "-q", "--no-index",
            "--find-links", _setup + "/wheels",
            "--target", _PYENV, "--ignore-installed",
            "vllm",
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    if _PYENV not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, _PYENV)
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
print("vllm", vllm.__version__)

-    lines = prefix.splitlines()

-        lines.pop()

+def clean_prefix(prefix: str) -> str:
+    # Keep only the leading run of genuine import/blank lines; stop at the first
+    # comment or other statement (that marks the start of any prior bootstrap).
+    kept = []
+    for ln in prefix.splitlines():
+        s = ln.strip()
+        if s == "" or s.startswith("import ") or s.startswith("from "):
+            kept.append(ln)
+        else:
+            break
+    while kept and kept[-1].strip() == "":
+        kept.pop()
+    return "\n".join(kept)

=== full corrected cell (a2) ===
import json
import math
import re
import subprocess

import kagglehub

# vLLM offline bootstrap. vLLM is absent from the base image; install it from the
# aimo-3-utils wheels bundle (py3.12 / cu128 / vllm 0.17.1) into a dedicated
# writable dir with --target, then put it FIRST on sys.path. Two pitfalls handled:
#  (1) the ryanholbrook/nvidia-utility-script mount puts a READ-ONLY `nvidia/`
#      namespace on sys.path, so a plain install fails merging nvidia-* (torch
#      CUDA) wheels into it -> --target keeps every file in /kaggle/tmp/pyenv.
#  (2) inserting a not-yet-existent dir on sys.path poisons the import finder
#      cache -> insert AFTER install and call importlib.invalidate_caches().
import importlib
import sys

_PYENV = "/kaggle/tmp/pyenv"
try:
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
    _arch = sorted(
        glob.glob("/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/aimo-3-utils*/wheels.tar.gz")
        + glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/wheels.tar.gz", recursive=True)
    )
    assert _arch, "aimo-3-utils wheels.tar.gz not attached (add it as a kernel source)"
    _setup = "/kaggle/tmp/setup"
    if not os.path.exists(_setup + "/wheels"):
        os.makedirs(_setup, exist_ok=True)
        subprocess.run(["tar", "-xzf", _arch[0], "-C", _setup], check=True)
    os.makedirs(_PYENV, exist_ok=True)
    subprocess.run(
        [
            "pip", "install", "-q", "--no-index",
            "--find-links", _setup + "/wheels",
            "--target", _PYENV, "--ignore-installed",
            "vllm",
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    if _PYENV not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, _PYENV)
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
print("vllm", vllm.__version__)

MODEL_PATH = kagglehub.model_download(
    "metric/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b-bf16/transformers/default"
)
SOUP_PATH = None
if USE_SOUP:
    _cfg = glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/adapter_config.json", recursive=True)
    assert _cfg, "USE_SOUP but soup adapter not found under /kaggle/input"
    SOUP_PATH = os.path.dirname(_cfg[0])
_train = glob.glob("/kaggle/input/competitions/*/train.csv") or glob.glob(
    "/kaggle/input/**/train.csv", recursive=True
)
assert _train, "train.csv not found"
print("model:", MODEL_PATH, "| soup:", SOUP_PATH, "| train:", _train[0])

=== sanity: _train defined in same cell as bootstrap? (B too) ===
True

```markdown
---
name: reference_vllm_offline_kaggle_blackwell
description: How to install vLLM offline in a Kaggle Blackwell (RTX Pro 6000) kernel that also mounts the read-only ryanholbrook nvidia util script — the 4 pitfalls.
metadata:
  type: reference
---

vLLM is **absent** from the nemo competition base image (`gcr.io/kaggle-private-byod/python@sha256:9fa0da…`, NvidiaRtxPro6000 / Blackwell, python3.12). The v11 rejection-sampling kernels (`nemo-v11-sample-a2` harry, `nemo-v11-sample-b` may) need it. Working recipe proven 2026-06-15 (kernel v6 ran past install+30B model-load+preflight, sustained RUNNING):

**Bundle:** attach `harrysun2006/aimo-3-utils-0171` as a **kernel source** (public; built via `pip download --python-version 3.12 --only-binary=:all: --extra-index-url …/whl/cu128 … vllm==0.17.1`). py3.12 + cu128 = Blackwell-compatible; vLLM 0.17.1 supports Nemotron-H (Mamba2+MoE, first-class since ~vLLM 0.15.1). The gpt-oss AIMO-3 kernels *ran* on H100 but the wheels were downloaded for cu128/py312, so they port to Blackwell. Fallback if a newer vLLM is needed: builder staged as `nemo-vllm-utils` (vllm 0.18.0, same flags).

**In-kernel bootstrap (4 pitfalls, all required):**
1. `import vllm` is absent → extract `…/aimo-3-utils*/wheels.tar.gz` to `/kaggle/tmp/setup` and pip-install from `…/wheels`.
2. The `ryanholbrook/nvidia-utility-script` mount (needed for the Blackwell ptxas/cutlass fix, B5) puts a **read-only `nvidia/` namespace on sys.path**, so a plain `pip install` dies merging `nvidia-*` (torch CUDA) wheels into it → install with `--target /kaggle/tmp/pyenv --ignore-installed`.
3. Inserting a not-yet-existent dir on `sys.path` poisons the import finder cache → insert `_PYENV` **after** install + `importlib.invalidate_caches()`.
4. vLLM inspects the model in a **subprocess** (`/usr/bin/python3 -m vllm.model_executor.models.registry`) that won't see the parent's `sys.path` → also `os.environ["PYTHONPATH"] = _PYENV + os.pathsep + …`.

Watch pushed kernels via `kaggle kernels status <id>` every ~3 min; logs only download after terminal state (`kaggle kernels output <id>`). A fast env failure ERRORs within ~6 min; surviving >~15 min RUNNING = past the fail-fast preflight. These v11 kernels are **post-competition data-gen (no submission)**. Related: [[reference_kaggle_dual_account]], [[reference_kaggle_input_paths]], [[reference_kaggle_stub_boundary]].

```

  A=$(KAGGLE_CONFIG_DIR="$HOME/.kaggle" kaggle kernels status harrysun2006/nemo-v11-sample-a2 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'KernelWorkerStatus\.[A-Z]*' | head -1)

  echo "[$TS] poll#$i  A2(harry)=$A  B(may)=$B"
  a_done=0; b_done=0
  case "$A" in *ERROR*|*COMPLETE*|*CANCEL*) a_done=1;; esac
  case "$B" in *ERROR*|*COMPLETE*|*CANCEL*) b_done=1;; esac
  if [ "$a_done" = 1 ] && [ "$b_done" = 1 ]; then echo "BOTH TERMINAL: A2=$A B=$B"; exit 0; fi
  sleep 1200
done
echo "completion watch ended (8h cap)"
EOF
echo "long watcher written"

../../worklogs/nemo2.md:1104:> - **Self-Distillation and Rejection Sampling**: Filtering for high-quality trajectories via rejection sampling significantly enhances fine-tuned model performance across diverse benchmarks compared to unfiltered baselines. ../../worklogs/nemo2.md:1106:> - **Synthetic Data**: Rejection sampling is used to construct a dataset of successful and executable reasoning trajectories for supervised fine-tuning, filtering for high-quality data by retaining only those trajectories that lead to correct outcomes.

import json

import kagglehub

# vLLM offline bootstrap. vLLM is absent from the base image; install it from the
# aimo-3-utils wheels bundle (py3.12 / cu128 / vllm 0.17.1) into a dedicated
# writable dir with --target, then put it FIRST on sys.path. Two pitfalls handled:
#  (1) the ryanholbrook/nvidia-utility-script mount puts a READ-ONLY `nvidia/`
#      namespace on sys.path, so a plain install fails merging nvidia-* (torch
#      CUDA) wheels into it -> --target keeps every file in /kaggle/tmp/pyenv.
#  (2) inserting a not-yet-existent dir on sys.path poisons the import finder
#      cache -> insert AFTER install and call importlib.invalidate_caches().
#  (3) vLLM inspects the model in a SUBPROCESS; --target is only on the parent's
#      sys.path, so also export PYTHONPATH so child processes import vllm.

# ruff: noqa: E402  (Kaggle kernel: imports follow env/setup cells)
# Nemo T12 — official-metric localization + min-logprob hard-val adapter ranking.
#
# Ports the official scorer (extract \boxed{}; fallback to last number; exact or numeric
# 1e-2) and builds a min-logprob "hardest-N-per-category" validation set from train.csv
# (base model assigns lowest gold-answer logprob = hardest). Then greedy-decodes each
# candidate LoRA adapter with the official params and ranks them by hard-val accuracy.
# NO submission here — output is a ranking JSON to choose which adapter to promote.
import glob
import site

_cutlass = glob.glob(
    "/kaggle/usr/lib/notebooks/ryanholbrook/*nvidia*util*/nvidia_cutlass_dsl/python_packages"
)
for _p in _cutlass:
    site.addsitedir(_p)

import os
import shutil
import stat as _stat

_ptxas = glob.glob(
    "/kaggle/usr/lib/notebooks/ryanholbrook/*/triton/backends/nvidia/bin/ptxas-blackwell"
)
if _ptxas:
    _dst = "/tmp/ptxas-blackwell"
    try:
        shutil.copy2(_ptxas[0], _dst)
        os.chmod(
            _dst, os.stat(_dst).st_mode | _stat.S_IEXEC | _stat.S_IXGRP | _stat.S_IXOTH
        )
        os.environ["TRITON_PTXAS_BLACKWELL_PATH"] = _dst
        os.environ["TRITON_PTXAS_PATH"] = _dst
        print("ptxas-blackwell ->", _dst)
    except OSError as _e:
        print("ptxas copy failed:", _e)

# %%
# Eval config. Hardest categories get more of the budget (bit/equation/cipher).
HARD_PER_CAT = {
    "bit": 16,
    "equation": 16,
    "cipher": 16,
    "numeral": 8,
    "gravity": 8,
    "unit": 8,
    "other": 8,
}
OFFICIAL_MAX_TOKENS = 7680  # official greedy decode budget
import time as _time

T0 = _time.time()
EVAL_DEADLINE_SEC = 25200  # 7h guard; always reach the ranking print

# %%
import json
import math
import re
import subprocess

import kagglehub

# vLLM offline bootstrap. vLLM is absent from the base image; install it from the
# aimo-3-utils wheels bundle (py3.12 / cu128 / vllm 0.17.1) into a dedicated
# writable dir with --target, then put it FIRST on sys.path. Two pitfalls handled:
#  (1) the ryanholbrook/nvidia-utility-script mount puts a READ-ONLY `nvidia/`
#      namespace on sys.path, so a plain install fails merging nvidia-* (torch
#      CUDA) wheels into it -> --target keeps every file in /kaggle/tmp/pyenv.
#  (2) inserting a not-yet-existent dir on sys.path poisons the import finder
#      cache -> insert AFTER install and call importlib.invalidate_caches().
#  (3) vLLM inspects the model in a SUBPROCESS; --target is only on the parent's
#      sys.path, so also export PYTHONPATH so child processes import vllm.
import importlib
import sys

_PYENV = "/kaggle/tmp/pyenv"
os.environ["PYTHONPATH"] = _PYENV + os.pathsep + os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
try:
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
    _arch = sorted(
        glob.glob("/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/aimo-3-utils*/wheels.tar.gz")
        + glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/wheels.tar.gz", recursive=True)
    )
    assert _arch, "aimo-3-utils wheels.tar.gz not attached (add it as a kernel source)"
    _setup = "/kaggle/tmp/setup"
    if not os.path.exists(_setup + "/wheels"):
        os.makedirs(_setup, exist_ok=True)
        subprocess.run(["tar", "-xzf", _arch[0], "-C", _setup], check=True)
    os.makedirs(_PYENV, exist_ok=True)
    subprocess.run(
        [
            "pip", "install", "-q", "--no-index",
            "--find-links", _setup + "/wheels",
            "--target", _PYENV, "--ignore-installed",
            "vllm",
        ],
        check=True,
    )
    if _PYENV not in sys.path:
        sys.path.insert(0, _PYENV)
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
    import vllm  # noqa: F401
print("vllm", vllm.__version__)

# %%
# ---- official metric (ported): extract \boxed{} else last number; exact or numeric 1e-2
_BOXED = re.compile(r"\\boxed\{([^}]*)(?:\}|$)")
_LZ = re.compile(r"0\d+")


def extract_final_answer(text):
    if not text:
        return "NOT_FOUND"
    m = _BOXED.findall(text)
    if m:
        ne = [x.strip() for x in m if x.strip()]
        return ne[-1] if ne else m[-1].strip()
    nums = re.findall(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?", text)
    return nums[-1] if nums else "NOT_FOUND"


def verify(gold, pred):
    gold, pred = str(gold).strip(), str(pred).strip()
    if not _LZ.fullmatch(gold) and not _LZ.fullmatch(pred):
        try:
            return math.isclose(float(pred), float(gold), rel_tol=1e-2, abs_tol=1e-5)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            pass
    return pred.lower() == gold.lower()


def classify(p):
    pl = p.lower()
    if "8-bit binary" in pl or "bit manipulation" in pl:
        return "bit"
    if "gravitational constant" in pl:
        return "gravity"
    if "unit conversion" in pl or "convert the following measurement" in pl:
        return "unit"
    if "secret encryption" in pl or "decrypt" in pl:
        return "cipher"
    if "numeral system" in pl:
        return "numeral"
    if "transformation rules is applied to equations" in pl:
        return "equation"
    return "other"


# %%
import csv

_train = glob.glob("/kaggle/input/competitions/*/train.csv") or glob.glob(
    "/kaggle/input/**/train.csv", recursive=True
)
assert _train, "train.csv not found"
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(_train[0], encoding="utf-8")))
for r in rows:
    r["category"] = classify(r["prompt"])
print(f"train rows: {len(rows)}")

MODEL_PATH = kagglehub.model_download(
    "metric/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b-bf16/transformers/default"
)
print("model:", MODEL_PATH)

# %%
# ---- discover candidate adapters from attached kernel-source / dataset mounts.
# Each entry: (label, adapter_dir). Resolve adapter_config.json; if only a
# submission.zip is present, unzip it into /kaggle/tmp/<label>.
import zipfile


def _resolve_adapter(label, roots):
    for root in roots:
        cfgs = glob.glob(root + "/**/adapter_config.json", recursive=True)
        if cfgs:
            return os.path.dirname(sorted(cfgs)[0])
    for root in roots:
        zips = glob.glob(root + "/**/submission.zip", recursive=True)
        if zips:
            dst = f"/kaggle/tmp/adapter_{label}"
            os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True)
            with zipfile.ZipFile(sorted(zips)[0]) as zf:
                zf.extractall(dst)
            cfgs = glob.glob(dst + "/**/adapter_config.json", recursive=True)
            if cfgs:
                return os.path.dirname(sorted(cfgs)[0])
    return None


CANDIDATE_ROOTS = {
    "soup": ["/kaggle/input/**/nemo-merge-soup*", "/kaggle/input/**/*merge-soup*adapter*"],
    "c1": ["/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/nemo-solver-c1*"],
    "c2": ["/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/nemo-solver-c2*"],
    "v15": ["/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/nemo-synth-v15*"],
    "v14": ["/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/nemo-replay-v14*"],
}
adapters = {}
for label, pats in CANDIDATE_ROOTS.items():
    roots = []
    for pat in pats:
        roots += glob.glob(pat)
    path = _resolve_adapter(label, roots) if roots else None
    if path:
        adapters[label] = path
        print(f"adapter {label}: {path}")
    else:
        print(f"adapter {label}: NOT FOUND (skipped)")
assert adapters, "no candidate adapters resolved; attach adapter kernel outputs/datasets"

# %%
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest

llm = LLM(
    model=str(MODEL_PATH),
    tensor_parallel_size=1,
    max_num_seqs=64,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,
    dtype="auto",
    max_model_len=8192,
    trust_remote_code=True,
    enable_lora=True,
    max_lora_rank=32,
)
tok = llm.get_tokenizer()
SUFFIX = (
    "\nPlease put your final answer inside \\boxed{}. For example: \\boxed{your answer}"
)


def build_prompt(p):
    return tok.apply_chat_template(
        [{"role": "user", "content": p + SUFFIX}],
        tokenize=False,
        add_generation_prompt=True,
        enable_thinking=True,
    )


# %%
# ---- min-logprob hard-val selection: score the gold answer's logprob under the BASE
# model (teacher-forced via prompt_logprobs); hardest = lowest summed logprob. Pick the
# hardest N per category. Fallback: if logprob scoring fails, take the first N per cat.
def _gold_logprob_prompts(batch):
    out = []
    for r in batch:
        base = build_prompt(r["prompt"])
        out.append(base + "\\boxed{" + str(r["answer"]).strip() + "}")
    return out


hard_rows = []
try:
    score_sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=1, prompt_logprobs=0)
    scored = []
    BATCH = 64
    # subsample to keep scoring bounded
    cand = [r for r in rows if r["category"] in HARD_PER_CAT]
    for i in range(0, len(cand), BATCH):
        if _time.time() - T0 > EVAL_DEADLINE_SEC // 3:
            print("logprob-scoring budget hit; using what we have")
            break
        b = cand[i : i + BATCH]
        outs = llm.generate(_gold_logprob_prompts(b), score_sp)
        for r, o in zip(b, outs):
            pls = o.prompt_logprobs or []
            tail = pls[-12:] if len(pls) > 12 else pls  # answer region (tail tokens)
            s = 0.0
            n = 0
            for pos in tail:
                if not pos:
                    continue
                lp = max(pos.values(), key=lambda x: x.logprob).logprob
                s += lp
                n += 1
            scored.append((s / n if n else 0.0, r))
        print(f"  scored {min(i + BATCH, len(cand))}/{len(cand)}")
    by_cat = {}
    for sc, r in scored:
        by_cat.setdefault(r["category"], []).append((sc, r))
    for cat, n in HARD_PER_CAT.items():
        items = sorted(by_cat.get(cat, []), key=lambda x: x[0])[:n]  # lowest logprob
        hard_rows += [r for _, r in items]
    print(f"min-logprob hard-val: {len(hard_rows)} rows")
except Exception as _e:  # noqa: BLE001
    print("logprob scoring failed, fallback to stratified:", _e)
    by_cat = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_cat.setdefault(r["category"], []).append(r)
    for cat, n in HARD_PER_CAT.items():
        hard_rows += by_cat.get(cat, [])[:n]

assert hard_rows, "empty hard-val set"
print("hard-val by category:", {c: sum(1 for r in hard_rows if r["category"] == c) for c in HARD_PER_CAT})

# %%
# ---- fail-fast preflight: one adapter, one problem must decode before the full grid.
_lbl0 = next(iter(adapters))
_lora0 = LoRARequest(_lbl0, 1, adapters[_lbl0])
_pf = llm.generate(
    [build_prompt(hard_rows[0]["prompt"])],
    SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, max_tokens=256),
    lora_request=_lora0,
)
assert _pf and _pf[0].outputs, "preflight produced no output"
print("preflight OK:", _pf[0].outputs[0].text[:100].replace("\n", " "))

# %%
# ---- rank every adapter on the hard-val set with the official decode params.
gen_sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, max_tokens=OFFICIAL_MAX_TOKENS)
prompts = [build_prompt(r["prompt"]) for r in hard_rows]
results = {}
for li, (label, apath) in enumerate(sorted(adapters.items())):
    if _time.time() - T0 > EVAL_DEADLINE_SEC:
        print("eval deadline hit; stopping")
        break
    lora = LoRARequest(label, li + 1, apath)
    outs = llm.generate(prompts, gen_sp, lora_request=lora)
    per_cat = {}
    correct = 0
    for r, o in zip(hard_rows, outs):
        ok = bool(o.outputs) and verify(r["answer"], extract_final_answer(o.outputs[0].text))
        correct += int(ok)
        d = per_cat.setdefault(r["category"], [0, 0])
        d[0] += int(ok)
        d[1] += 1
    acc = correct / len(hard_rows)
    results[label] = {
        "overall_acc": acc,
        "n": len(hard_rows),
        "per_category": {c: f"{v[0]}/{v[1]}" for c, v in per_cat.items()},
    }
    print(f"[{label}] hard-val acc = {acc:.4f}  per-cat={results[label]['per_category']}")

# %%
ranking = sorted(results.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]["overall_acc"], reverse=True)
out_path = "/kaggle/working/t12_hardval_ranking.json"
with open(out_path, "w") as f:
    json.dump(
        {"hard_val_n": len(hard_rows), "results": results,
         "ranking": [k for k, _ in ranking]}, f, indent=2
    )
print("=== T12 hard-val ranking (best first) ===")
for k, v in ranking:
    print(f"  {k}: {v['overall_acc']:.4f}  {v['per_category']}")
print("wrote", out_path)
print("Done.")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Convert a percent-format (.py with `# %%` cell markers) script to a Kaggle .ipynb.
Usage: py2ipynb.py <in.py> <out.ipynb>
"""
import json
import sys

src = open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8").read()
lines = src.splitlines(keepends=True)

cells = []
cur = []
for ln in lines:
    if ln.rstrip("\n") == "# %%":
        if cur:
            cells.append(cur)
        cur = []
    else:
        cur.append(ln)
if cur:
    cells.append(cur)

# strip leading/trailing blank lines per cell; drop empties
nb_cells = []
for c in cells:
    while c and c[0].strip() == "":
        c.pop(0)
    while c and c[-1].strip() == "":
        c.pop()
    if not c:
        continue
    nb_cells.append(
        {"cell_type": "code", "execution_count": None, "metadata": {}, "outputs": [], "source": c}
    )

nb = {
    "cells": nb_cells,
    "metadata": {
        "kernelspec": {"display_name": "Python 3", "language": "python", "name": "python3"},
        "language_info": {"name": "python"},
    },
    "nbformat": 4,
    "nbformat_minor": 5,
}
json.dump(nb, open(sys.argv[2], "w"), indent=1)
print(f"wrote {sys.argv[2]} with {len(nb_cells)} code cells")

```

def run_training() -> None:
    """Reproduce the public fresh rank-32 Replay-Math LoRA recipe."""
    import gc
    import json
    import math
    import random
    import sys
    import time

    from unsloth import FastLanguageModel

  case "$B" in *ERROR*|*COMPLETE*|*CANCEL*) echo "B TERMINAL: $B"; exit 0;; esac
  sleep 600
done
echo "watch_any ended (8h cap)"
EOF

# ---- discover candidate adapters from attached kernel-source / dataset mounts.
# Each entry: (label, adapter_dir). Resolve adapter_config.json; if only a
# submission.zip is present, unzip it into /kaggle/tmp/<label>.
import zipfile


def _resolve_adapter(label, roots):
    for root in roots:
        cfgs = glob.glob(root + "/**/adapter_config.json", recursive=True)
        if cfgs:
            return os.path.dirname(sorted(cfgs)[0])
    for root in roots:
        zips = glob.glob(root + "/**/submission.zip", recursive=True)
        if zips:
            dst = f"/kaggle/tmp/adapter_{label}"
            os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True)
            with zipfile.ZipFile(sorted(zips)[0]) as zf:
                zf.extractall(dst)
            cfgs = glob.glob(dst + "/**/adapter_config.json", recursive=True)
            if cfgs:
                return os.path.dirname(sorted(cfgs)[0])
    return None


CANDIDATE_ROOTS = {
    "soup": [
        "/kaggle/input/**/nemo-merge-soup*",
        "/kaggle/input/**/*merge-soup*adapter*",
    ],
    "c1": ["/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/nemo-solver-c1*"],
    "c2": ["/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/nemo-solver-c2*"],
    "v15": ["/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/nemo-synth-v15*"],
    "v14": ["/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/nemo-replay-v14*"],
}
adapters = {}
for label, pats in CANDIDATE_ROOTS.items():
    roots = []
    for pat in pats:
        roots += glob.glob(pat)
    path = _resolve_adapter(label, roots) if roots else None
    if path:
        adapters[label] = path
        print(f"adapter {label}: {path}")
    else:
        print(f"adapter {label}: NOT FOUND (skipped)")
assert adapters, (
    "no candidate adapters resolved; attach adapter kernel outputs/datasets"
)

# %%
from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest

#### 🔎 WebSearch `LoRA adapter SVD singular value amplification scaling improve performance inference`

`12:07:13`

> I've found several relevant research papers and resources on LoRA adapters with SVD-based techniques for improving performance. Here are the key findings:
> 
> ## SVD-Based LoRA Improvements
> 
> **Initialization Methods:**
> Initializing LoRA with SVD of the pretrained weights accelerates convergence in the early stages of LoRA training. Retaining the top singular vectors consistently yields better performance across various tasks.
> 
> **Spectral Surgery Approach:**
> Spectral Surgery is a training-free refinement that decomposes a LoRA update with SVD, estimates per-component sensitivity using gradients on a small calibration set, and reweights singular values under a magnitude constraint while keeping the learned directions fixed. Spectral Surgery yields consistent gains (up to +4.4 points on CommonsenseQA and +2.4 pass@1 on HumanEval) by adjusting only ~1,000 scalar coefficients.
> 
> **Adaptive SVD Methods:**
> Singular-value initialization is widely used in LoRA to preserve pre-trained weight characteristics, with PiSSA only updating the largest singular values, while MiLoRA adjusts minor singular values for strong performance.
> 
> **LoRA-XS:**
> LoRA-XS achieves extreme parameter efficiency by setting LoRA's projection matrices using Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of the pre-trained module weights and keeping them frozen during training.
> 
> **Scaling Factors:**
> The setting of the scaling factor in LoRA is overly aggressive and causes gradient collapse as the rank increases, which slows learning.

---

- [LoRA-XS: Low-Rank Adaptation with Extremely Small Number of Parameters](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.17604v3)
- [Spectral Surgery: Training-Free Refinement of LoRA via Gradient-Guided Singular Value Reweighting](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.03995)
- [Make LoRA Great Again: Boosting LoRA with Adaptive Singular Values and Mixture-of-Experts Optimization Alignment](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.16894v3)
- [A Rank Stabilization Scaling Factor for Fine-Tuning with LoRA](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.03732)
- [LoRA · Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/docs/peft/package_reference/lora)
- [GOAT: Bridging the LoRA vs. Full Fine-Tuning Gap with Adaptive MoE and SVD | by Lakhan Malviya | Medium](https://medium.com/@lakhanmalviya_91647/goat-bridging-the-lora-vs-full-fine-tuning-gap-with-adaptive-moe-and-svd-0b2635144194)

> Based on the search results, here's what I found about merging LoRA adapters and the various methods available in 2025:
> 
> ## Overview of LoRA Merging Methods
> 
> LoRA merging involves combining multiple LoRA adapters to create a more versatile model.
> 
> ## Key Merging Approaches
> 
> **Task Arithmetic:** Task Arithmetic introduces the concept of task vectors—the difference between weights of a model trained on a task and a pretrained model—and shows it's possible to perform basic operations on such vectors to achieve multi-tasking by adding up task vectors of task-specific models.
> 
> **TIES-Merging:** TIES-Merging builds upon Task Arithmetic by operating on parameters of task vectors and discarding small delta parameters, merging only parameters shared among the majority.
> 
> **DARE:** DARE extends this idea but simplifies it significantly by dropping around 90% of delta parameters. More specifically, DARE discards the vast majority of parameter changes—up to 90-99%—on the premise that most updates are not essential, and the remaining updates are then amplified to preserve the overall scale of the modification.
> 
> **Model Soups:** While merging focuses on resolving conflicts between model weights, souping explores optimal proportions for combining ingredient models.
> 
> ## Recent Advances (2025)
> 
> Recent research has explored newer methods including KnOTS, which uses SVD to align LoRA adapter subspaces before merging, improving upon naive averaging for task-to-task merging. Additionally, TaDA outperforms all baselines, including DARE-TIES and Task Arithmetic, while introducing zero inference overhead.

#### 🔎 WebSearch `Spectral Surgery training-free LoRA singular value reweighting calibration set method`

`12:08:13`

> Based on the search results, here's what I found about Spectral Surgery:
> 
> Spectral Surgery is a training-free refinement framework that keeps the learned directions fixed and reallocates capacity within the low-rank space by reweighting singular values using lightweight calibration signals (gradient-projection sensitivities) under conservative magnitude/energy control.
> 
> The method decomposes a LoRA update with SVD, estimates per-component sensitivity using gradients on a small calibration set, and reweights singular values under a magnitude constraint while keeping the learned directions fixed.
> 
> The key insight behind this approach is that in residual-writing projections, the learned singular sub-spaces are comparatively stable and task-aligned, while the learned spectrum can be inefficient or even detrimental, emerging as a primary post-training bottleneck.
> 
> Spectrum-only editing can yield clear task-dependent gains while modifying only O(r) scalars per module.
> 
> This research appears in the paper "Spectral Surgery: Training-Free Refinement of LoRA via Gradient-Guided Singular Value Reweighting," with more details available on arXiv (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.03995).

> I found several highly relevant results about STaR (Self-Taught Reasoners), rejection sampling, self-distillation, and the saturation/diminishing returns challenges:
> 
> ## Key Findings:
> 
> **Diminishing Returns with Rejection Sampling:**
> Although rejection sampling methods can improve data quality, they do not guarantee correct intermediate steps. As a result, scaling up CoT data has diminishing returns, with gains nearing saturation—e.g., OpenMathInstruct-2 only sees a 3.9% boost on MATH despite an 8× increase in dataset size.
> 
> **Self-Distillation Saturation:**
> A critical theoretical bottleneck in self-distillation is the rapid onset of policy saturation. After a few iterations of SPIN or OPSD, empirical observations universally note a plateau or severe degradation. Because the student optimizes against a target sharing its own inductive biases and architectural limitations, the hypothesis space progressively collapses.
> 
> **Overcoming Saturation:**
> Interestingly, the first Self-Distillation phase saturates around step 400; after teacher synchronization, a second phase yields at least 3 additional percentage points without signs of saturation.
> 
> **STaR Framework:**
> LLMs can improve their capabilities by training on self-generated data, characterizing them as self-taught reasoners (STaRs). For mathematical reasoning, pioneer studies generally follow an iterative process: (1) generating candidate responses for a given math problem via temperature sampling; (2) selecting responses based on answer correctness; and (3) updating the model using either SFT or DPO.

"""Local port of the competition's grading logic (T12).

Mirrors the official metric so local evaluation matches the leaderboard:
  - extract the LAST `\\boxed{...}`; if absent, fall back to "final answer is:" patterns,
    then to the last number in the text (the grader's documented fallbacks);
  - a prediction is correct if it matches the gold answer EXACTLY as a string
    (case-insensitive) OR numerically within a 1e-2 relative tolerance.

Pure functions only (no model / GPU). The generation half of the official `score()`
(vLLM greedy, `max_tokens=7680`, `temp=0`) runs inside the kernel; this module is the
extract+verify+accuracy half so a local held-out set can be scored the same way the LB
scores it. Source of the rules: competition evaluation page + the embedded scorer in the
public `lopure/amplify-...` notebook (see `references.md`).

Usage:
    from official_metric import extract_final_answer, verify, accuracy
    acc = accuracy(gold_list, raw_model_outputs)   # raw outputs -> extract -> verify
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import re

_BOXED = re.compile(r"\\boxed\{([^}]*)(?:\}|$)")
_FALLBACK_PATTERNS = [
    r"final answer is:?\s*([^\n]+)",
    r"final answer\s*[:：]\s*([^\n]+)",
    r"answer is:?\s*([^\n]+)",
]
_NUMBER = re.compile(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?")


def extract_final_answer(text: str | None) -> str:
    """Extract the final answer from raw model output, mirroring the official extractor."""
    if text is None:
        return "NOT_FOUND"

_LEADING_ZERO_INT = re.compile(
    r"0\d+"
)  # e.g. binary "01000011" — leading zero is significant


def verify(gold: str, predicted: str) -> bool:
    """True if predicted matches gold.

    Numeric comparison (rel 1e-2) is used ONLY when neither side is a leading-zero
    integer; binary/leading-zero answers are string-matched so `01000011` != `1000011`
    (the official metric's fixed binary behaviour). Strings are case-insensitive.
    """
    gold = str(gold).strip()
    predicted = str(predicted).strip()
    if not _LEADING_ZERO_INT.fullmatch(gold) and not _LEADING_ZERO_INT.fullmatch(
        predicted
    ):
        try:
            return math.isclose(
                float(predicted), float(gold), rel_tol=1e-2, abs_tol=1e-5
            )
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            pass
    return predicted.lower() == gold.lower()


def accuracy(golds, raw_outputs) -> float:
    """Accuracy over raw model outputs: extract each then verify against gold."""
    golds = list(golds)
    raw_outputs = list(raw_outputs)
    if not golds:
        return 0.0
    correct = sum(
        verify(g, extract_final_answer(o)) for g, o in zip(golds, raw_outputs)
    )
    return correct / len(golds)

_BOXED = re.compile(r"\\boxed\{([^}]*)(?:\}|$)")
_FALLBACK_PATTERNS = [
    r"final answer is:?\s*([^\n]+)",
    r"final answer\s*[:：]\s*([^\n]+)",
    r"answer is:?\s*([^\n]+)",
]
_NUMBER = re.compile(r"-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?")
_LEADING_ZERO_INT = re.compile(r"0\d+")


def extract_final_answer(text):
    if text is None:
        return "NOT_FOUND"
    matches = _BOXED.findall(text)
    if matches:
        non_empty = [m.strip() for m in matches if m.strip()]
        return non_empty[-1] if non_empty else matches[-1].strip()
    for pat in _FALLBACK_PATTERNS:
        m = re.findall(pat, text, re.IGNORECASE)
        if m:
            return m[-1].strip()
    nums = _NUMBER.findall(text)
    if nums:
        return nums[-1]
    lines = [ln.strip() for ln in text.splitlines() if ln.strip()]
    return lines[-1] if lines else "NOT_FOUND"


def verify(gold, predicted):
    gold = str(gold).strip()
    predicted = str(predicted).strip()
    if not _LEADING_ZERO_INT.fullmatch(gold) and not _LEADING_ZERO_INT.fullmatch(
        predicted
    ):
        try:
            return math.isclose(float(predicted), float(gold), rel_tol=1e-2, abs_tol=1e-5)
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            pass
    return predicted.lower() == gold.lower()


def classify(p):
    pl = p.lower()
    if "8-bit binary" in pl or "bit manipulation" in pl:
        return "bit"
    if "gravitational constant" in pl:
        return "gravity"
    if "unit conversion" in pl or "convert the following measurement" in pl:
        return "unit"
    if "secret encryption" in pl or "decrypt" in pl:
        return "cipher"
    if "numeral system" in pl:
        return "numeral"
    if "transformation rules is applied to equations" in pl:
        return "equation"
    return "other"

soup_config = json.load(open(SOUP_CFG))
print("soup LoRA r/alpha:", soup_config.get("r"), soup_config.get("lora_alpha"))

# %%
# ---- spectral surgery: rewrite the soup state dict per a reweighting config ----
def _refactor(B, A, reweight_fn):
    """Efficient rank-r SVD of delta = B@A (B:[out,r], A:[r,in]); reweight singular
    values via reweight_fn(S)->S'; re-factor to (B',A') with B'@A' = U diag(S') V^T.
    Rank (r columns) preserved. All math in float32 on CPU."""
    Bf = B.float()
    Af = A.float()
    Qb, Rb = torch.linalg.qr(Bf)          # Qb:[out,r], Rb:[r,r]
    Qa, Ra = torch.linalg.qr(Af.T)        # Af.T:[in,r] -> Qa:[in,r], Ra:[r,r]
    M = Rb @ Ra.T                          # [r,r]; delta = Qb @ M @ Qa.T
    U, S, Vh = torch.linalg.svd(M)         # U:[r,r], S:[r], Vh:[r,r]
    S2 = reweight_fn(S)
    left = Qb @ U                          # [out,r]
    right = Qa @ Vh.T                      # [in,r]
    sq = torch.sqrt(S2.clamp(min=0.0))
    B2 = left * sq.unsqueeze(0)            # [out,r]
    A2 = (right * sq.unsqueeze(0)).T       # [r,in]
    return B2, A2


def _make_reweight(cfg):
    mode = cfg["mode"]
    if mode == "scale":
        c = float(cfg["scale"])
        return lambda S: S * c
    if mode == "energy":
        e = float(cfg["energy"])
        amp = float(cfg["amp"])

        def fn(S):
            order = torch.argsort(S, descending=True)
            S_sorted = S[order]
            energy = (S_sorted**2).cumsum(0)
            total = energy[-1].clamp(min=1e-12)
            keep_sorted = (energy / total) <= e
            keep_sorted[0] = True  # always keep the top component
            out = torch.zeros_like(S)
            out[order] = torch.where(keep_sorted, S_sorted * amp, torch.zeros_like(S_sorted))
            return out

        return fn
    return lambda S: S  # identity


def build_variant(cfg, src_state, out_dir):
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    reweight = _make_reweight(cfg)
    target_mods = cfg.get("modules")  # None => all modules
    new_state = {}
    a_keys = [k for k in src_state if k.endswith("lora_A.weight")]
    touched = 0
    for ak in a_keys:
        bk = ak[: -len("lora_A.weight")] + "lora_B.weight"
        A = src_state[ak]
        B = src_state[bk]
        do_it = cfg["mode"] != "identity" and (
            target_mods is None or any(m in ak for m in target_mods)
        )
        if do_it:
            B2, A2 = _refactor(B, A, reweight)
            new_state[ak] = A2.to(A.dtype).contiguous()
            new_state[bk] = B2.to(B.dtype).contiguous()
            touched += 1
        else:
            new_state[ak] = A.clone()
            new_state[bk] = B.clone()
    # carry over any non-lora tensors verbatim (e.g., embeddings if present)
    for k, v in src_state.items():
        if k not in new_state:
            new_state[k] = v.clone()
    save_file(new_state, os.path.join(out_dir, "adapter_model.safetensors"))
    json.dump(soup_config, open(os.path.join(out_dir, "adapter_config.json"), "w"))
    return touched


print("loading soup state dict (cpu)...")
SOUP_STATE = load_file(SOUP_ST, device="cpu")
_n_pairs = sum(1 for k in SOUP_STATE if k.endswith("lora_A.weight"))
print(f"soup tensors: {len(SOUP_STATE)} ({_n_pairs} lora_A/B pairs)")

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
from vllm.lora.request import LoRARequest

llm = LLM(
    model=str(MODEL_PATH),
    tensor_parallel_size=1,
    max_num_seqs=64,
    gpu_memory_utilization=0.85,
    dtype="auto",
    max_model_len=8192,
    trust_remote_code=True,
    enable_lora=True,
    max_lora_rank=int(soup_config.get("r", 32)),
)
tok = llm.get_tokenizer()
SUFFIX = (
    "\nPlease put your final answer inside \\boxed{}. For example: \\boxed{your answer}"
)
GEN = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, max_tokens=7680)
prompts = [
    tok.apply_chat_template(
        [{"role": "user", "content": r["prompt"] + SUFFIX}],
        tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True,
    )
    for r in rows
]


def eval_adapter(adapter_dir, lora_id):
    lora = LoRARequest(f"v{lora_id}", lora_id, adapter_dir)
    outs = llm.generate(prompts, GEN, lora_request=lora)
    per_cat = {}
    correct = 0
    for r, o in zip(rows, outs):
        ok = bool(o.outputs) and verify(r["answer"], extract_final_answer(o.outputs[0].text))
        correct += int(ok)
        d = per_cat.setdefault(r["category"], [0, 0])
        d[0] += int(ok)
        d[1] += 1
    return correct / len(rows), {c: f"{v[0]}/{v[1]}" for c, v in per_cat.items()}


# %%
# fail-fast preflight: build the identity variant + score 2 prompts (validates the
# surgery -> save -> vLLM-load path before the full sweep).
_pf_dir = "/kaggle/tmp/variant_preflight"
build_variant({"name": "pf", "mode": "identity"}, SOUP_STATE, _pf_dir)

                   lora_request=LoRARequest("pf", 999, _pf_dir))
assert _pf and _pf[0].outputs, "preflight produced no output"
print("preflight OK:", _pf[0].outputs[0].text[:80].replace("\n", " "))
shutil.rmtree(_pf_dir, ignore_errors=True)

# %%
# ---- sweep configs: build -> eval -> keep best (one variant on disk at a time) ----
BEST_DIR = "/kaggle/working/best_adapter"
results = {}
best_name, best_acc = None, -1.0
for i, cfg in enumerate(SURGERY_CONFIGS):
    if _time.time() - T0 > EVAL_DEADLINE_SEC:
        print("deadline hit; stopping sweep")
        break
    vdir = f"/kaggle/tmp/variant_{i}"
    touched = build_variant(cfg, SOUP_STATE, vdir)
    acc, per_cat = eval_adapter(vdir, i + 1)
    results[cfg["name"]] = {"acc": acc, "per_category": per_cat, "modules_touched": touched}
    print(f"[{cfg['name']}] hard-val acc = {acc:.4f}  touched={touched}  per-cat={per_cat}")
    if acc > best_acc:
        best_acc, best_name = acc, cfg["name"]
        shutil.rmtree(BEST_DIR, ignore_errors=True)
        shutil.copytree(vdir, BEST_DIR)
    shutil.rmtree(vdir, ignore_errors=True)

print(f"\nBEST: {best_name}  acc={best_acc:.4f}")

    with zipfile.ZipFile(sub, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:
        zf.write(os.path.join(BEST_DIR, "adapter_config.json"), "adapter_config.json")
        zf.write(os.path.join(BEST_DIR, "adapter_model.safetensors"), "adapter_model.safetensors")
    with zipfile.ZipFile(sub) as zf:
        names = set(zf.namelist())
        assert names == {"adapter_config.json", "adapter_model.safetensors"}, names
    h = hashlib.sha256(open(sub, "rb").read()).hexdigest()
    print(f"WROTE submission.zip ({os.path.getsize(sub) / 1e9:.2f} GB) sha256={h}")
    print(f"  -> surgery '{best_name}' beat soup baseline {base_acc:.4f} -> {best_acc:.4f}")
else:
    print(f"No surgery variant beat the soup baseline ({base_acc:.4f}); "
          "NOT writing submission.zip (hold the 0.86 soup).")
print("Done.")

```
