# Final-sprint research + chosen directions (nemo, 2026-06-15, ~12h to deadline)

> Goal: push past our standing best **0.86** (own-work SVD soup v14+c1+b1) in the last window.
> Inputs: T12 hard-val ranking (soup/v14 robust; c1/c2/v15 regress hard cipher/bit; `equation`
> unsolved by all ≤2/16), a competition-research sweep (forum/code/HF/arXiv), and slot/time limits
> (deadline 2026-06-15 23:59 UTC; quota won't reset before close).

## Research synthesis (cited; trust labelled)

**Cheap post-hoc lever — spectral / SVD surgery on a trained adapter (no training):**
- **Spectral Surgery** ([arXiv 2603.03995](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.03995), trusted) — SVD-decompose each LoRA delta, **reweight singular values** (keep directions fixed) under an energy constraint, calibrated on a small set; "+2–4 pts", "the learned spectrum is a primary post-training bottleneck", modifies O(r) scalars, **rank-preserving**. Corroborated by [Make LoRA Great Again](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16894), [Primacy of Magnitude in LoRA](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2507.06558).
- **lopure's notebook** "amplify-top-50-singular-value-retain-84.4%-energy" ([Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/code/lopure/amplify-top-50-singular-value-retain-84-4-energy), community/low — title only; code JS-rendered) — a competition instance of the above on a Nemotron adapter: keep top singular vectors to 84.4% cumulative energy, amplify, applied to all LoRA modules. ⚠ Caveat: amplifying a well-calibrated adapter *can* hurt; risk is bounded (LB keeps the max) and it's gated locally on hard-val here.

**Merge methods** ([survey](https://loraexchange.ai/guides/merging_adapters/)): DARE (drop ~90% deltas + amplify), TIES (sign-align/trim), KnOTS (SVD-align subspaces) can beat a plain weighted soup — but T12 shows our augmented members (c1/c2/v15) are weak on hard problems, so re-merging them mostly dilutes; the merge ceiling from the existing pool is ~0.86–0.87.

**Frontier — the `equation`/`bit` categories (the 0.85→0.87+ differentiator):**
- The proven public pattern is **solver-guided teacher CoT**: brute-force the hidden rule from the examples, then a strong teacher writes a CoT that *states the rule first* — qualitatively stronger than our template/synth CoT. Publicly available pre-made in [andy279/nemotron-reasoning-challenge](https://huggingface.co/datasets/andy279/nemotron-reasoning-challenge) (trusted_public): 50,455 correct-only traces incl. ~2,703 solver-guided bit+transformation traces (teachers: DeepSeek V3.2, Nemotron-Super-120B, GPT-5.4). Reported ~0.87 territory (inferred).
- **kuangyicheng short-format alignment (~0.87)** ([discussion #703896](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/nvidia-nemotron-model-reasoning-challenge/discussion/703896), community/medium): long-CoT replay adapters can hit `max_new_tokens=7680` *before* emitting `\boxed{}` on hard problems → empty answer. ~240-step fine-tune on SHORT responses re-aligns the format and recovers them.

**Against more self-distillation (validates the v11 stand-down):** rejection-sampling CoT shows "diminishing returns near saturation" and self-distillation hits "rapid policy saturation/degradation — the student shares the teacher's biases" ([on-policy distillation survey](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.00626), [Why Self-Distillation Degrades Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.24472v2)). Only an *external* teacher breaks the plateau.

**Rules (⚠ verify on the official page):** synthetic data generation is explicitly permitted; external-model-generated CoT + public HF datasets appear allowed and were used by competitors without apparent DQ. Hard constraint = rank≤32 LoRA, real training (no weight repack). External-teacher CoT (andy279) is a *different compliance posture* than our prior own-work CoT — get explicit human OK before relying on it.

## Chosen directions

| # | Account | Direction | Why | Compliance | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | harrysun2006 | **Spectral/SVD surgery on the 0.86 soup** (`nemo-surgery-a`) — sweep global-scale + top-energy-amplify (incl. lopure's e=0.844) + Mamba-only configs; score each on the fixed hard-val with the official metric; package the best-beating-soup variant. | Highest-confidence path to 0.87–0.89 (lopure precedent + Spectral Surgery). Post-hoc, **no training**, ~1–2h, rank-preserving. | ✅ own-work transform of our own adapter | cheap |
| **B** | firefly2006 | **Solver-guided bit/equation teacher-CoT adapter** (andy279 subset) — fresh v14-recipe LoRA + the ~2,703 solver-guided hard-cat traces; submit standalone and/or soup with v14. Attacks the only unsolved frontier (`equation`). | Highest *ceiling* — the documented 0.85→0.87 lever; orthogonal to A. | ⚠ external-teacher CoT — **needs human OK on rules** | ~7h + 1 may slot |

Deliberately NOT pursued: another v11 stage-2 SFT (T5 — cipher-heavy + self-distillation saturation), generic merge-search (capped, dilutive per T12).

## Status
- **A pushed** (`harrysun2006/nemo-surgery-a` v1) — running; gated to only emit `submission.zip` if a variant beats the soup on hard-val (never regress the banked 0.86).
- **B held** pending the human compliance call on external-teacher (andy279) training data.
- Submissions to the leaderboard remain gated on explicit human approval (CLAUDE.md).

> # Nemotron Reasoning Challenge Dataset Schema
> 
> ## Main Format (SFT Data)
> 
> The primary dataset uses a chat message structure:
> 
> ```json
> {
>   "messages": [
>     {"role": "user", "content": "[puzzle prompt]"},
>     {"role": "assistant", "content": "<think>[reasoning]</think>\boxed{answer}"}
>   ]
> }
> ```
> 
> **Key fields in messages:**
> - `role`: "user" or "assistant"
> - `content`: prompt text or reasoning + boxed answer
> 
> ## Raw Traces Format
> 
> The `all_traces_merged.jsonl` file contains additional metadata:
> 
> - `id`: puzzle identifier
> - `prompt`: full puzzle text
> - `ground_truth`: correct answer
> - `attempts`: array of attempt objects with:
>   - `reasoning`: step-by-step explanation
>   - `content`: model output
>   - `predicted_answer`: extracted final answer
>   - `is_correct`: correctness flag
>   - `temperature`: sampling parameter
> - `usage`: token counts
> 
> ## Config/Split Names
> 
> Load with: `datasets.load_dataset("andy279/nemotron-reasoning-challenge")`
> - **Splits**: `train`, `validation`
> - **Default config**: (none specified; single unnamed config)
> 
> ## Category Information
> 
> No explicit "category" column in SFT data. Categories exist only in metadata descriptions (bit_manipulation, cipher, gravity, etc.). The raw traces file would contain source/teacher model information, though specific field names for filtering aren't documented in this excerpt.
> 
> **Filtering note**: The page doesn't expose specific column names for identifying "solver-guided" traces or category types within the loaded dataset structure.

# Nemo andy279 prep — fetch the public solver-guided teacher-CoT subset (internet ON).
# Downloads andy279/nemotron-reasoning-challenge (correct-only SFT traces from external
# teachers: DeepSeek V3.2 / Nemotron-Super-120B / GPT-5.4), classifies each by prompt,
# and saves ONLY the hard categories (bit / equation / cipher) as a JSONL the offline
# training kernel attaches. Human-authorized 2026-06-15 (external-teacher CoT; rules
# permit synthetic/external data — verify the official rules page before final submit).
import json
import re
import subprocess
import sys

subprocess.run(
    [sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "datasets", "huggingface_hub"],
    check=True,
)
from datasets import load_dataset


def classify(p):
    pl = (p or "").lower()
    if "8-bit binary" in pl or "bit manipulation" in pl:
        return "bit"
    if "gravitational constant" in pl:
        return "gravity"
    if "unit conversion" in pl or "convert the following measurement" in pl:
        return "unit"
    if "secret encryption" in pl or "decrypt" in pl:
        return "cipher"
    if "numeral system" in pl:
        return "numeral"
    if "transformation rules is applied to equations" in pl:
        return "equation"
    return "other"


_BOXED = re.compile(r"\\boxed\{([^}]*)(?:\}|$)")
KEEP_CATS = {"bit", "equation", "cipher"}

ds = load_dataset("andy279/nemotron-reasoning-challenge", split="train")
print("andy279 train rows:", len(ds))
print("example keys:", list(ds[0].keys()))

kept = []
by_cat = {}
for ex in ds:
    msgs = ex.get("messages")
    if not msgs or len(msgs) < 2:
        continue
    user = next((m.get("content") for m in msgs if m.get("role") == "user"), None)
    asst = next((m.get("content") for m in msgs if m.get("role") == "assistant"), None)
    if not user or not asst:
        continue
    if not _BOXED.search(asst):  # require a \boxed{} answer in the response
        continue
    cat = classify(user)
    if cat not in KEEP_CATS:
        continue
    kept.append({"category": cat, "prompt": user, "response": asst})
    by_cat[cat] = by_cat.get(cat, 0) + 1

out_path = "/kaggle/working/andy279_hardcat.jsonl"
with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    for rec in kept:
        f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
print(f"kept {len(kept)} hard-cat teacher CoTs by category: {by_cat}")
print("wrote", out_path)

    # ---- v11 stage-2: rejection-sampled, ground-truth-verified CoT --------------

    # answer already matches train.csv). Reconstruct each training example as the exact
    # sampled sequence: prompt tokens (chat template, enable_thinking=True, matching the
    # sampler) + cot tokens + EOS, with response-only masking (prompt weights = 0). This
    # avoids re-wrapping the raw <think>…\boxed{} generation through the chat template.
    import glob as _glob

    _corpus = sorted(
        _glob.glob("/kaggle/input/notebooks/*/nemo-v11-sample-*/verified_cot.jsonl")
        + _glob.glob("/kaggle/input/**/verified_cot.jsonl", recursive=True)
    )
    assert _corpus, "v11 verified_cot.jsonl not found (attach nemo-v11-sample-b output)"
    print(f"v11 corpus: {_corpus[0]}")
    _eos = tokenizer.eos_token_id
    SUFFIX = (
        "\nPlease put your final answer inside \\boxed{}. "
        "For example: \\boxed{your answer}"
    )

    def _prompt_ids_thinking(problem):
        # Tokenize WITH the template's special tokens (tokenize=True), matching how the
        # replay/huikang examples above are built via _template_ids — so the v11 prompt
        # tokens are consistent with the rest of the corpus. enable_thinking mirrors the
        # v11 sampler's prompt; fall back if the template doesn't accept the kwarg.
        msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": problem + SUFFIX}]
        try:
            out = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
                msgs, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True
            )
        except TypeError:
            out = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
                msgs, tokenize=True, add_generation_prompt=True
            )
        if hasattr(out, "keys"):
            out = out["input_ids"]
        if out and isinstance(out[0], (list, tuple)):
            out = out[0]
        return list(out)

    solver_examples: list[dict] = []
    _sv_skipped = 0
    _sv_first = False
    _by: dict = {}
    with open(_corpus[0], encoding="utf-8") as _cf:
        for line in _cf:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            rec = json.loads(line)
            cot = rec.get("cot") or ""
            if not cot.strip():
                _sv_skipped += 1
                continue
            prompt_ids = _prompt_ids_thinking(rec["prompt"])
            cot_ids = list(tokenizer(cot, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"])
            if _eos is not None:
                cot_ids = cot_ids + [_eos]
            full_ids = prompt_ids + cot_ids
            if len(full_ids) > MAX_SEQ_LEN:
                # keep the prompt and right-truncate the CoT tail (lose EOS) only if
                # forced; skip if truncation would drop the whole response.
                full_ids = full_ids[:MAX_SEQ_LEN]
                if len(full_ids) <= len(prompt_ids):
                    _sv_skipped += 1
                    continue
            prompt_len = min(len(prompt_ids), len(full_ids))
            mask = [0] * prompt_len + [1] * (len(full_ids) - prompt_len)
            if len(full_ids) < 2 or not any(mask[1:]):
                _sv_skipped += 1
                continue
            cat = rec.get("category", "other")
            _by[cat] = _by.get(cat, 0) + 1
            if not _sv_first:
                _sv_first = True
                print(
                    f"v11 row 0 ({cat}): prompt_ids={len(prompt_ids)}, "
                    f"full_ids={len(full_ids)}"
                )
            solver_examples.append(
                {
                    "problem_id": "v11_" + cat,
                    "tokens": full_ids[:-1],
                    "targets": full_ids[1:],
                    "weights": [float(m) for m in mask[1:]],
                }
            )
    print(f"v11 verified per-category: {_by} (total {len(solver_examples)})")
    assert len(solver_examples) >= MIN_V11_EXAMPLES, (
        f"only {len(solver_examples)} v11 examples (skipped={_sv_skipped}); "
        f"expected at least {MIN_V11_EXAMPLES}."
    )
    sv_every = max(1, len(examples) // len(solver_examples))
    woven: list[dict] = []
    si = 0
    for i, ex in enumerate(examples):
        woven.append(ex)
        if (i + 1) % sv_every == 0 and si < len(solver_examples):
            woven.append(solver_examples[si])
            si += 1
    woven.extend(solver_examples[si:])
    examples = woven
    print(
        f"v11 self-distillation: {len(solver_examples)} verified examples woven "
        f"(skipped={_sv_skipped}, every ~{sv_every}); total now {len(examples)}"
